**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Summary**

The primary equipment failure was **Turbine T-4**, taken offline on 14 March 2025 after its bearing seal corroded through and allowed seawater into the nacelle (root cause: corrosion of the bearing seal housing). 

Over the full 24-month operating period, the pilot delivered **18.7 GWh** to the grid—6% below the original forecast of 19.9 GWh.

The project finished at **EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million**, a 12.4% overrun (EUR 4.55 million) driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

On the environmental front, an independent fish-monitoring programme compared migration counts before and after installation and found **no statistically significant change** (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer **Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fasteners with duplex stainless steel** on all remaining nacelles—a change the steering group accepted in principle.

**Final decision:** The steering group approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
